transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-08-07
Start time: 15:30 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Mills (Redwood AE), Priya Gupta (Redwood SE), Daniel Kim (Acme - Head of ML), Maria Lopez (Acme - Platform Eng), Sanjay Patel (Acme - Security), Ethan Park (Acme - Product)

Summary (auto):
Quick console walkthrough focusing on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Discussed Hosted vs Dedicated economics, per-route cost attribution, caching/batching impacts, and compliance questions. Agreed next steps: pricing, benchmark template, and pilot scheduling.

Topics:
- Console: per-route dashboards and filters
- Usage analytics: token-level vs request-level billing, retention, alerts
- Cost breakdown: per-route, per-model, per-tenant cost views, sample spreadsheet
- Routing & fallbacks: dedicated vs hosted, private deployment notes
- Compliance: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, SSO

Action items (recap in call):
- Jordan: send pricing and Dedicated quote
- Priya: share benchmark template and dashboard export
- Acme (Daniel): share traffic profile and SLOs
- Sanjay: provide SOC2 questionnaire responses

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan Mills from Redwood, AE on the account. We'll do a 30-ish minute walkthrough of the console and then leave time for questions and next steps. Priya's gonna show the per-route dashboards.
[00:18] Priya: hi, hi, thanks. So jumping into the Redwood Consoel — excuse me, console — we're on the demo tenant, first screen is the Usage Analytics overview. You can see overall token consumption, request counts, and cost estimates for the period.
[00:35] Maria: quick question, does that cost calc include our custom quantized models or is that only for hosted redwood models?
[00:45] Priya: good call, the estimate pulls from whichever model variant you're using. If you're on a Dedicated pool using a privately hosted quantized model the cost line will show the model variant but the unit economics are based on your Dedicated pricing. The UI will mark dedicated vs hosted. Sometimes the transcription or label shows "dedicated pool" as "dedicated p" — ignore the small UX typo.
[01:10] Daniel: can you show per-route breakdowns? we have different routes, some low-latency features, some batch jobs.
[01:18] Priya: yep. Route-level dashboards are here. You can filter by route name, tag, or model. We surface token-level cost, request-level cost, average latency p50/p95, error rates, and conversion to dollar amounts. There's an export to CSV and a sample per-route billing sheet we can share.
[01:41] Jordan: note that per-route attribution is an approximation when you have shared caches or batching — we try to attribute based on request origin and namespace. If you use prefix caching or KV cache the effective per-token cost drops and that shows up as "cache hit savings" in the panel.
[02:02] Daniel: how accurate is the cost split when batching is in play? our batch jobs coalesce 4 requests routinely.
[02:12] Priya: good point. Batching is accounted for at the runtime level; the UI attributes tokens to the originating requests by weight, but there can be edge cases where a single large batch spans routes — we annotate those with a small delta and flag them for manual audit. We'll include notes in the sample sheet.
[02:35] Maria: what about retention? we don't want raw transcripts kept longer than 30 days in your logs.
[02:42] Jordan: you can configure retention per-tenant; Hosted defaults to 90 days but you can request 30-day retention or turn on no-logs for certain routes. For Private/Dedicated we can support customer-managed retention and empty logs via the VPC option.
[03:05] Sanjay: and KMS? where are keys managed for private deploys?
[03:10] Priya: Dedicated and Private support KMS/HSM integrations — you control keys. We'll add the KMS integration doc link in the follow-up.
[03:22] Ethan: show me an example of a cost spike and how we would investigate it.
[03:27] Priya: sure, jump to alerts. here's a spike on 2025-07-28, we can click into the route and see the request timeline, top prompts, and token distribution. You can pivot by model or by user id. The trace links into the request inspector and you can pull the exact prompt (redacted per retention policy).
[03:53] Daniel: is there an easy way to map cost back to product features for chargeback?
[04:00] Priya: yep, we recommend tagging routes with feature and team labels. The per-route export includes tags so finance can map to cost centers. We also have an API endpoint that returns per-route cost data for automation.
[04:20] Maria: is that API public or part of Redwood Dedicated?
[04:25] Jordan: it's available on Hosted and Dedicated; for Dedicated you get more granularity and longer retention windows.
[04:34] Ethan: can we set alerts on p95 or cost thresholds?
[04:38] Priya: yes, alerting is in the Console — you can create alerts for p50/p95, token spend thresholds, or unusual error rates. Alerts can notify Slack, PagerDuty, or send a webhook.
[04:56] Sanjay: compliance — are audit logs immutable? we need chain-of-custody for admin actions.
[05:02] Priya: audit logs are write-once in Hosted, with export-to-S3 for Dedicated/Private. We support SAML/SSO, RBAC, and granular admin roles. We'll include the compliance pack in the follow-up.
[05:25] Jordan: quick piece on Optimize features — the console surfaces model/quantization recommendations per workload. For example, a high-throughput embedding route might be recommended to move to a quantized variant which can reduce cost by 40% with negligible quality loss.
[05:43] Daniel: do you show expected quality deltas? we need to ensure prompt-level quality not degraded.
[05:49] Priya: yes, Optimize includes eval snapshots — we tie quality regressions to prompt sets and show A/B metrics and hallucination indicators. You can roll back model variants through the rollout UI.
[06:08] Maria: what's the rollout UX look like? can we canary by region or by percent?
[06:12] Priya: you can do canary by percentage and by route, and you can pin by region or customer tier. There are automatic fallback policies to previous model versions if latency or error thresholds breach.
[06:30] Jordan: bringing this back to pricing: Hosted is pay-as-you-go; Dedicated is reserved capacity with a monthly commit and lower per-token price. We'll send a sample quote. For customers with regulatory constraints we discussed Private with VPC and KMS.
[06:51] Daniel: what's the delta in price roughly? numbers would be helpful now though I know you've got to send a quote.
[06:58] Jordan: ballpark, Dedicated can be 30-60% cheaper per-token depending on utilization and chosen GPU types; the sample spreadsheet will show breakpoints.
[07:12] Maria: do you support mixed routing — some traffic on Hosted and overflow to Dedicated?
[07:18] Priya: yes, smart routing can overflow to hosted or to cheaper model variants. You can set policies based on latency SLOs, cost, or region.
[07:30] Daniel: any mention of fallback to smaller models for non-critical features?
[07:35] Priya: exactly — prime example: you can set a routing policy to use a cheaper quantized model for background summarization and keep the higher-quality model for interactive chat. The console shows estimated cost impact if you change routing.
[07:53] Jordan: let's demo a live per-route cost breakdown. I'm going to filter to the "search-summarize" route. You can see tokens by day, model used, and the cost column that aggregates GPU unit economics, overhead, and caching savings.
[08:14] Priya: note the "cache savings" badge — that's from KV/prefix caching. If you enable prefix cache for that route you can shave off a lot of tokens for repeated prompts.
[08:27] Daniel: does Redwood run the KV store or do we manage it?
[08:31] Priya: by default it's managed (hosted) but Dedicated supports customer-managed KV in your VPC for privacy sensitive workloads.
[08:40] Maria: for pilot purposes can we run sample traffic to measure real cost?
[08:44] Jordan: yes, we typically run a 1-week pilot with your traffic on a mirror or sampled traffic — we run detailed benchmarking and provide a report. That was the 2-week or 1-week pilot? we can be flexible.
[09:01] Ethan: On the bench, do you emulate our batching behavior?
[09:05] Priya: yes, you'll provide the traffic profile and batching patterns; our benchmarking harness will replay it and measure throughput/latency/cost.
[09:14] Daniel: great. On security again, how does SSO provisioning work for our teams?
[09:19] Jordan: SAML/SCIM provisioning is supported; we can provision groups and roles. For Dedicated/Private you can enforce stricter RBAC and tie to AD.
[09:30] Sanjay: encryption at rest for model weights and KV?
[09:33] Priya: weights in Dedicated are stored encrypted with customer-managed keys if you choose KMS; KV can be configured similarly.
[09:40] Maria: what about cost per embedding vs text gen, are those unified?
[09:45] Priya: console normalizes units but the breakdown separates embeddings vs generation. Embeddings often billed per vector or per token depending on model; we'll include the mapping in the sample pricing spreadsheet.
[09:58] Jordan: quick aside, the "per-route cost forecast" button projects spend for next 30 days based on current usage and any scheduled rollouts. Useful for finance.
[10:10] Daniel: nice. can that export be pushed into our billing system?
[10:14] Priya: yes, we have a billing API and webhooks for daily cost dumps.
[10:20] Maria: in the per-route UI is there a view that links to raw request traces?
[10:24] Priya: there's a request inspector. You can open individual requests (redacted) and see prompt, model, latency timeline, and kernel-level notes the runtime may attach.
[10:38] Daniel: kernel-level notes? like GPUs and kernels used?
[10:42] Priya: yes sometimes the runtime annotates the kernel/quantization path chosen, e.g., int8-path or memory-optimized kernel; that helps debug perf regressions. There's occasional transcription noise that reads it as "kernal" in older exports.
[10:58] Jordan: moving on, let's discuss Optimize recommendations — right now this route gets a suggestion to move to a 4-bit quantized variant with caching for repeated prompts, expected cost delta ~43% with a slight p95 increase of 20ms in our internal eval.
[11:18] Maria: can we preview the eval prompts?
[11:21] Priya: yes — Optimize stores eval snapshots and you can see quality metrics per prompt set. You can also attach your own golden prompts for regression monitoring.
[11:33] Ethan: any way to automate route-level rollbacks on quality regressions?
[11:36] Priya: you can configure automatic rollback triggers on quality or latency thresholds.
[11:42] Sanjay: I see notes about audit retention and export — is the audit export tamper-evident?
[11:48] Priya: exports are signed and can be pushed to your S3 with versioning enabled. For dedicated we can enable write-once S3 buckets.
[12:00] Jordan: ok let's talk about a concrete pilot. Priya will run the benchmark once we get your traffic profile, aim for a 1-week run mirrored to a dedicated pool, and we'll provide a cost/latency report. Sound good?
[12:12] Daniel: yes. timeline wise we want results before our Q4 planning in late September.
[12:18] Jordan: we should aim for an early September pilot; we'll send calendar options.
[12:24] Maria: do you have any case studies for similar sized customers?
[12:28] Jordan: yes, we'll attach a short case study where a customer moved non-critical summarization to a quantized model and dropped costs ~50%.
[12:35] Daniel: competitor question — how do you differ from OpenAI here?
[12:39] Jordan: two main differences: unified serving across hosted/dedicated/private with routing and first-class per-route cost tooling; and the Optimize toolkit that suggests quantization/rollouts tied to evals. We also focus on production SLAs.
[12:54] Maria: any limitations on model types or custom ops?
[12:58] Priya: we support a broad set of open models and custom variants; some exotic operator graphs might require kernel work but our onboarding team helps.
[13:10] Ethan: ok let's walk through sending the artifacts — can you drop the deck and pricing in our shared drive?
[13:15] Jordan: we'll send the deck and the compliance pack. Also we'll include the sample per-route billing sheet and the bench harness template.
[13:23] Daniel: who will own the pilot on Redwood side?
[13:26] Jordan: Priya will own the technical side and I'll be the commercial owner — you'll see both on the calendar invite.
[13:33] Sanjay: last security Q: do you support customer-managed HSM?
[13:38] Priya: yes for Private deployments we support customer HSMs and dedicated key material. For Dedicated we offer KMS integrations.
[13:47] Maria: can you summarize next steps and timelines?
[13:50] Jordan: sure — recap: Jordan sends pricing and Dedicated quote by 2025-08-10; Priya sends bench template and sample dashboards by 2025-08-12; Acme provides traffic profile and SLOs by 2025-08-14; Sanjay returns SOC2 questions by 2025-08-11. We'll schedule the pilot for the week of 2025-09-01.
[14:16] Daniel: perfect. thanks everyone.
[14:18] Jordan: thanks, we'll follow up via email with the artifacts.
[14:22] Priya: thanks all.

(End of recording - some short sections omitted for brevity; transcription contains occasional mis-hearings like 'Consoel' and 'kernal').
